scope: Determine whether host 221 TCP source-port mapping is endpoint-independent, using two independent public observers and real SYN packets. Not a G2/S6 claim.

method.client: ssh root@192.168.1.221 'python3 /tmp/mapped_connect.py' - binds TCP socket to 0.0.0.0:19910, connects to two distinct public IPs on already-allowed port 22
observers: tcpdump -ni eth0 on 82.157.68.159 (independent public IP, internal 10.2.0.16)
tcpdump -ni eth0 on 119.29.150.254 (independent public IP, internal 10.1.0.2)
method.filter: tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0 and src host 112.5.60.4 and tcp port 22

mapping_axis.verdict: endpoint-independent mapping (EIM) for these two destinations at this instant

interpretation: 221 TCP source port 19910 is mapped to a single public port (here 20811) regardless of destination IP. The earlier 18011 was the mapping port for that earlier session; the port can change between sessions but is consistent across destinations within a session. This is the prerequisite for telling the peer to connect to the discovered port instead of 19910.
boundaries: Two destinations only; strong EIM evidence but not an exhaustive NAT taxonomy proof.
TCP EIM evidence does not imply 222 TCP EIM; 222 remains symmetric and must stay the active connector.
Mapping lifetime is finite; discovered port must be used promptly while the mapping is alive.
Does not by itself establish a TCP punch or any G2/S6 gate.
